title: State Monopolies
description: The companies most blamed for high prices and anti-consumer behavior are often the ones most protected from replacement. That protection requires a specific mechanism: a government grant.

title: Intellectual Property
description: Patent, copyright, and trademark are called property rights. They function as monopolies over ideas and expression, enforced at state expense, regardless of merit, at everyone else's cost.

title: Cognitive Capture
description: The people most invested in explaining why a system is broken are usually the same people most invested in the system staying broken. The explanation that leaves out the mechanism is not accidental.

title: Urban Planning
description: Car dependency, housing scarcity, and neighborhood segregation by income were built by planners acting on explicit theories. They are policy outputs, not market outcomes.

title: Technology & Sovereignty
description: Platform monopolies look like market outcomes. They are maintained by network effects, switching costs, and occasional government grants. Who owns the infrastructure determines who uses it, and on what terms.

title: Electoral Systems
description: The incumbent two-party cartel has survived every reform movement aimed at it. The survival strategy is to write the rules, specifically the ones that decide who gets on the ballot.
